articles.title: Joint Press Release : South Pacific Defence Ministers’ Meeting
articles.body:
Joint Press Release : South Pacific Defence Ministers’ Meeting
Defence ministers and representatives from Australia, Chile, Fiji, France, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and Tonga gathered in Nadi for the 11‘h South Pacific Defence Ministers’ Meeting (SPDMM) from 22 to 24 September 2026. They were joined by observers from Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States. Ms Desna Solofa, Acting Secretary General of the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) attended as a special guest.
Discussions focused on Securing the Blue Pacific: Collective Responsibility, Resilient Futures. Ministers recommitted to continue to work together to safeguard the region from traditional, non-traditional and hybrid security threats.
Ministers expressed grave concern over the recent ballistic missile test conducted into the waters of the Blue Pacific, which occurred without appropriate notice. Ministers noted that this was the second such test in the region within two years. Ministers highlighted that the manner in which this activity was conducted risked undermining PIF Leaders’ declaration of the Blue Pacific Continent as an Ocean of Peace. lt also undermined Leaders’ call to engage with the Blue Pacific Continent in a manner that honours the Pacific Way, respects national sovereignty and supports national and Pacific-led approaches. Ministers echoed the statement by Leaders at the 55‘h PIF Leaders’ Meeting.
In response to an intelligence brief from the Oceania Directorates of Military Intelligence Meeting (ODMIM), Ministers noted the compounding impacts of El Niño and the fuel crisis on the Pacific security environment, as well as transnational and serious organised crime and cyber.
Regional preparedness and collective action
Ministers reflected on the evolution of the Pacific Response Group (PRG) into a genuinely regional asset following its successful rotation of headquarters to New Zealand (1 July 2026) and now year round co-location. They welcomed the Commander of the PRG's update on achievements of the PRG since SPDMM 2025, notably participation in a Certification Exercise (28 October to 6 November 2025) and Exercise MARARA June 2026). Ministers welcomed Fiji's expression of interest to host the PRG from July 2028. Ministers agreed to take a phased approach to expanding the mandate of the PRG, recognising the importance of first consolidating and enhancing the PRG's humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) capabilities, before working to include stabilisation operations guided by comprehensive regional consultations and supported by appropriate legal frameworks.
Ministers acknowledged the range of exercises conducted under the POVAI ENDEAVOUR Framework in 2026 to build interoperability. Ministers thanked Chile for its update on the strategic planning underway for Exercise Taina Vaikava and looked forward to updates at SPDMM 2027.
Ministers also thanked Australia for its report on the Joint Heads of Pacific Security gHoPS) meeting that it hosted in April 2026. They requested that they continue to be updated on relevant developments, particularly the Regional Operations Deployment Framework (RODF). Ministers tasked the Chiefs and Heads of Defence (CHODs) to take back to the JHoPS meeting a request that any future RODF consider the privileges and immunities relevant to HADR and any future PRG stabilisation function, subject to endorsement by PIF leaders.
Ministers welcomed the update on progress towards a SPDMM Status of Forces Agreement and tasked the Intersessional Working Group (IWG) to commence formal negotiations in line with national processes.
Ministers visited the Blackrock peacekeeping and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief camp and received a briefing and tour showcasing Fiji's operations in support of peacekeeping, HADR and countering TNOC.
Ministers agreed that the SPDMM remains the most effective forum to pursue military peacekeeping cooperation in the South Pacific and identified a number of peacekeeping initiatives to further explore through the IWG.
Ministers recognised the growing challenges of emerging technology, cyber security and artificial intelligence and tasked the IWG to explore how defence organisations could better cooperate in these areas.
Maritime security
Ministers welcomed the presentation from Fiji on transnational organised crime (TNOC). Ministers noted TNOC has intensified in the region and reaffirmed their commitment to jointly responding to detect, deter and disrupt TNOC across the maritime domain. Ministers noted that at the 55‘h PIF Leaders' Meeting, a regional mechanism \/Vaqa Moana was agreed in principle to strengthen collective maritime security response, information sharing and regional resilience. Ministers tasked CHODs to explore a potential future SPDMM contribution to regional efforts such as \/Vaqa Moana and report back at SPDMM 2027.
Regional partnerships and coordinating with regional architecture
Ministers conveyed their sincere appreciation to the acting PIF Secretary General Ms Desna Solofa for attending the meeting as a special guest. Ministers endorsed an update to the Governance Framework to include a standing invitation to the PIF Secretary General. Ministers welcomed the regional perspective Ms Solofa had brought to the discussions and thanked the PIF Secretariat for presenting its Regional Peace and Security Action Plan 2026-2030. Ministers noted that the SPDMM Secretariat had been engaging as a member of the Peace and Security Pillar Thematic Advisory Group and had contributed to consultations on the Regional Peace and Security Action Plan. Ministers welcomed the ongoing collaboration between the SPDMM Secretariat and the PIF to explore how a SPDMM Defence Advisor position in the PIF Secretariat could contribute to the PIF's peace and security pillar of work.
Ministers recognised the existential threat posed by climate change and reflected on the role of defence forces in reducing emissions and supporting adaptation. Ministers also welcomed the brief from the PIF Climate Peace and Security Advisor on the regional climate peace and security agenda and encouraged the SPDMM Secretariat's ongoing consultation in light of Fiji's proposal for a SPDMM Climate Peace and Security Advisor at SPDMM 2025.
Ministers thanked New Zealand for its leadership on enhancing regional defence architecture through existing mechanisms. Ministers noted SPDMM Secretaries' intention to meet annually and thanked Fiji for its leadership to establish this initiative.
Thematic engagement initiatives
Recognising that women play a critical role in preventing conflict, building peace and helping countries recover during crises, ministers acknowledged their leadership and contributions to inclusive responses to Pacific security challenges. Ministers thanked Fiji for sharing the outcomes of its Gender Barrier Assessment, the region's first. Ministers noted the SPDMM Women Peace and Security Guidance Note, endorsed the priority recommendations and tasked the Secretariat and IWG to create a Forward Work Plan for implementation. Ministers encouraged members to share experiences.
Ministers thanked Fiji for hosting the third Pacific Defence Faith Forum in Nadi from 22 to 26 March 2026. Ministers welcomed the continued evolution of the Pacific Defence Faith Network, underpinned by people-to-people connections and faith-based engagement. Ministers recognised the important role that faith and spirituality plays in supporting sailors, soldiers and aviators, families and the communities in which they serve. They looked forward to the next forum in 2027.
Ministers looked forward to Fiji hosting emerging leaders in 2027 for the fourth South Pacific Defence Future Leaders' Summit.
Ministers welcomed an update on the Academic Cooperation Network (ACN), including its first live webinar and thanked Chile for its leadership for the next publication in 2027.
Ministers welcomed the launch of the Defence Training Hub-Pacific which integrated the SPDMM Regional Training Framework, an online platform designed to improve coordination of individual training courses available to personnel across the SPDMM community. Ministers welcomed an update on progress responding to Fiji's proposal to establish an environmental sustainability module.
Ministers thanked Fiji for hosting SPDMM 2026 and agreed that Australia would host SPDMM in 2027.

articles.title: Russia sends nuclear warning to Nato over its Kaliningrad enclave
articles.body:
Advertisement
Russia sends nuclear warning to Nato over its Kaliningrad enclave
Bilateral ties have sharply worsened, with European governments accusing Moscow of stepping up sabotage and arson acts on the continent
2-MIN READ2-MIN
 Listen
Russia has warned Nato it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if the Western alliance attempted to cut off Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave that borders the Baltic Sea.
In a document sent to Nato and seen by Reuters, Moscow accused the alliance of a “dangerous and reckless course” that entailed “high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict”.
The document said this included the possibility of “Russian strikes against decision-making centres in the alliance’s member states right from the outset”.

articles.title: Modi, Trump discuss India-US trade, defense, energy ties
articles.body:
Ahmad Adil
30 September 2026•Update: 30 September 2026
 Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday discussed India-US trade, defense and energy ties during a phone call with US President Donald Trump.
Modi wrote on US social media company X that he had a “productive conversation” with Trump.
“We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas,” Modi said, adding that they agreed to maintain “close engagement to take our comprehensive global strategic partnership forward.”
The call came days after the US enacted the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which allows the US president to impose targeted tariffs of up to 100% on imported goods from countries that buy the vast majority of Russian oil or gas and enable Russian sanctions evasion. New Delhi has raised concerns with Washington over the law.
Modi also said they “exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security.”
The talks came as India’s trade minister began a visit to the US for negotiations with American officials.
The US and India announced in February that they had reached terms on an interim framework deal aimed at resolving a bilateral trade dispute. Tensions had escalated last year over 50% tariffs imposed on Indian goods by the Trump administration, partly over India’s continued purchases of Russian oil amid the Russia-Ukraine war.
Bilateral trade between the two countries, which maintain a comprehensive global strategic partnership, totaled around $149.4 billion in 2025, according to officials.

articles.title: Russian diplomat warns about consequences of deploying Western troops in Ukraine
articles.body:
VIENNA, September 30. /TASS/. Russia would regard the deployment of Western troops in Ukraine as NATO forces appearing on its borders, with all the consequences that entails, Head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna Negotiations on Military Security and Arms Control Yulia Zhdanova said.
"We view the idea of deploying a Western military contingent in a neighboring country negatively and will regard it as NATO troops appearing on our borders, with all the consequences that entails," the diplomat said at a meeting of the OSCE Forum for Security Co-operation.
The diplomat said that the current policies of European governments are clearly aimed at preparing their defense industries, state apparatuses, economies and civilian infrastructure for aggressive action against Russia.

articles.title: South Africa urges men to take more responsibility for gender-based violence after series of killings
articles.body:
South Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders.
Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. He said police would be reviewing unsolved murders, attempted murders and serious sexual offences against women and children, as well as producing a funded plan to reduce the forensic backlog for such cases, both within 60 days.
In a televised speech on Tuesday night, the president said local governments would have five months to address issues that compromised women’s safety, from broken streetlights to overgrown public spaces and abandoned buildings. He added that he had tasked five ministers to come up with a plan within 60 days to reduce alcohol-fuelled violence.
“Alcohol does not cause gender-based violence and it can never excuse it. Responsibility always lies with the perpetrator,” Ramaphosa said. “But harmful alcohol use is a significant aggravating factor in interpersonal violence and it must be addressed as part of our wider prevention effort.
“Women should not have to live in fear because government has failed to repair a light, clear a public space, process evidence or enforce a law.”
South Africa has been gripped with grief and fury after the discovery of 11 women’s bodies dumped across Ekurhuleni, the municipality adjoining Johannesburg to the east, since 15 July. Eight of the women were found in the last three weeks, including Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, who was discovered on 12 September after she went missing when she went for a run after work.
Ramaphosa said suspects had been arrested in connection with three of the killings and that the other cases would not be left to go cold. He added that police had not found evidence that a serial killer was responsible for all 11 killings, but that all possibilities were still being investigated.
He also directly addressed South African men, urging them to challenge relatives, friends and colleagues who harass, humiliate or abuse women. “It is time for good men to stop being silent men,” he said.
“For too long, gender-based violence has been treated as a woman’s problem to solve. Women march, the women of our country organise, they speak out, they protest, they confront and they comfort survivors,” Ramaphosa said.
“Women change their routes home. Avoid going out at night and warn one another about dangerous places and dangerous men. We have placed the burden of male violence on women. That must change.”
Activists expressed their frustration that solid policy actions had not been taken years ago and scepticism that the measures Ramaphosa announced would work.
Shenilla Mohamed, the executive director of Amnesty International South Africa, said: “These are not new issues and as a country we have been talking about ways to tackle the high numbers of [gender-based violence and femicide], especially since 2019 when women took to the streets to protest, and yet here we are again in the face of continued attacks against women.
“Amnesty International South Africa also notes the timelines put in place by the president, but this will only mean something if it results in action, and if there are consequences for inaction.”
Mpiwa Mangwiro-Tsanga and Bafana Khumalo of Sonke Gender Justice, a NGO, said: “Our concern … is that the response remains heavily weighted towards what happens after violence has already occurred.”
They added: “Investigating unresolved cases, processing forensic evidence and repairing unsafe public spaces are necessary, but they do not constitute a comprehensive prevention strategy. It is concerning that the president is asking municipalities to do what is actually their mandate and yet they do not deliver on these.”

articles.title: Spain, France align on welcoming UK back to EU, strengthening China trade defences
articles.body:
Spain, France align on welcoming UK back to EU, strengthening China trade defences
MADRID, Sept 30 - Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and France's President Emmanuel Macron expressed enthusiasm on Wednesday for Britain rejoining the EU, and agreed Europe must strengthen its trade defences against China.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham floated the prospect of Britain rejoining the EU in an interview earlier on Wednesday, which Macron described as "excellent news" and a "good decision".
"We would open our arms [to Britain]," Sanchez said.
Speaking after Macron's first state visit to Spain, Sanchez described the neighbouring countries as leaders of Europe's "resistance to enemies of our continent and the European model", as both nations gear up for elections next year in which the far right is expected to make significant gains.
The two leaders also called for greater flexibility in finding additional resources for the bloc ahead of EU budget negotiations in October, with Sanchez appealing for "a little more empathy" from Brussels for governments "on the frontlines trying to respond to citizens' concerns".
Spain and France are among a group of countries concerned that the pressure from major net contributors to the EU budget such as Germany and the Netherlands to cut available funds by several hundred billion euros would worsen inequality and reduce funds for farmers, a key election issue.
Asked about the EU's ongoing negotiations over protecting industry from Chinese competition, the two leaders underscored the importance of securing commitments from Chinese investors on technology transfer in key industries like autos, where Spain's efforts to attract Chinese investors have prompted concern from some stakeholders about a lack of safeguards.
"On both sides of the Pyrenees we have actors who need to be protected when they suffer unfair competition...if we are not united as Europeans, we have no possibility of success," Macron said. REUTERS

articles.title: Man suspected of shooting prison warden knew victim from jail
articles.body:
Man suspected of shooting prison warden knew victim from jail
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The man accused of shooting dead a prison warden on a packed restaurant terrace in Amsterdam had spent time in a jail where the 61-year-old man worked, prosecutors confirmed on Monday.
Marcel Blijd died after being shot outside De Baanderij restaurant on the NDSM quay, on the north bank of the IJ, on Saturday afternoon. Dozens of people, some of them children, witnessed the incident.
The public prosecution service said the suspected gunman, 37-year-old Amin D., appeared to have reacted to a comment Blijd made referring to his detention in Zaandstad prison. Staff at the jail described Blijd as a “father figure” to staff and prisoners alike.
D. appeared in court on Monday before a magistrate, who ordered him to be detained for another 14 days on suspicion of murder.
The prosecution said in a statement that Blijd had spoken to D. on the terrace just before the shooting. “After a short conversation … the suspect left the terrace, but he returned shortly afterwards and shot the victim several times.”
Video footage showed the gunman made no attempt to flee, but flung the pistol into the water and surrendered to police when they arrived a few minutes later.
